newsitem.title: ITALY: One quarter of Austria phones mobile by 2000 - Stet.
newsitem.headline: One quarter of Austria phones mobile by 2000 - Stet.

text.p: Italian telecoms holding Stet, which on Wednesday announced a strategic partnership with Austria's Mobilkom, forecast that mobile phones would account for one quarter of the Austrian market by 2000.

Managing director Tomaso Tommasi di Vignano said in a statement that the deal would give Stet entry into a "promising and dynamic market with a penetration rate, for mobile phones, forecast to go from 8.75 percent now to 25 percent in the year 2000".

Austria's post and telecoms monopoly PTA said earlier that Stet had offered to buy a 25 percent stake in its Mobilkom Austria unit. The deal is subject to regulatory clearance by the European Commission.

It said Stet had offered 8.4 billion schillings ($697 million). Mobilkom operates Austria's biggest global system for mobile communications. Stet controls Telecom Italia Mobile, Europe's biggest mobile phone group. ($1=12.04 Austrian Schillings)
